title: Catalog manager (merge / archive / recategorize)
goal: A fallback screen for when automatic canonicalization got it wrong: consolidate two catalog_items that turn out to be the same real-world product (reassigning every reference, archiving the loser, recomputing stats from the now-combined history), fix a wrong or uncategorized item, and archive items no longer bought -- exactly the cleanup E-3's matching ladder deliberately deferred here (sub-S-09.json's out_of_scope).
in_scope: lib/catalog/manager.ts: getCatalogManagerItems() -- a lean, household-scoped query returning EVERY catalog_items row (archived included, with an isArchived flag) with canonicalName, brand, categoryName, isStaple, aliasCount, movementCount, lastPurchasedAt. Deliberately not a reuse of getInventoryItems() (which hard-filters is_archived=false) -- this screen's entire unarchive path requires archived rows to be visible, and its list doesn't need getInventoryItems()'s stock/prediction joins.

lib/catalog/manager.ts: getMergePreview(itemAId, itemBId) -- alias count and stock_movements count for each of the two selected items, so the merge confirm dialog can show 'combine N purchases and M aliases into one item' before the user commits (the UX journey doc's explicit friction point: merge must show a low-risk preview first).

Migration: merge_catalog_items(p_household_id uuid, p_survivor_id uuid, p_loser_id uuid) returns table(out_survivor_id uuid, out_reassigned_movements integer, out_reassigned_aliases integer). Locks both rows (select ... for update), rejects p_survivor_id = p_loser_id, rejects either row not found in p_household_id, rejects the survivor being archived, rejects the loser already being archived. Reassigns catalog_item_id on item_aliases, stock_movements, price_history, receipt_lines.matched_item_id, and shopping_list_items from loser to survivor, every UPDATE additionally scoped by household_id = p_household_id (deliberate defense-in-depth, not incidental, matching this repo's ADR-0004 convention even though the row-level lock already guarantees both ids belong to this household). plan_entries has a unique (household_id, catalog_item_id) index (S-21's migration) -- if the survivor already has a plan_entries row, the loser's is deleted rather than reassigned (survivor's entry wins); otherwise it's repointed, both branches household-scoped.

purchase_count carry-forward: captures each item's current item_stats.purchase_count (coalesce 0) BEFORE any delete, deletes item_stats_history for both ids and item_stats for the loser only, then inserts-or-updates the survivor's item_stats row with purchase_count = survivor_count + loser_count (upsert, so this works whether or not the survivor had an item_stats row yet -- e.g. a survivor with zero prior purchases merging in a loser that had some). This is the one field the downstream recompute cannot derive (lib/predictions/recompute.ts's toRow() deliberately never writes purchase_count, per its own comment -- it's owned by the commit paths), so the RPC must set it explicitly or it silently reverts to the survivor-only count (or 0, if a fresh row gets inserted by recompute's own upsert without this step running first).

Archives the loser (catalog_items.is_archived = true) -- never a hard delete (would break every FK this function just finished reassigning past, plus REQUIRED per this epic's own destructive-action guardrail: archiving is additive/reversible, hard-delete is not).

lib/catalog/manager.ts: mergeCatalogItems(survivorId, loserId) wraps the RPC then calls recomputeOneItem(survivorId, householdId) unconditionally afterward (no rateCorrectionOverride -- same invariant as every other purchase-adjacent recompute call in this repo) so the survivor's ewma/cadence/confidence reflect the full combined stock_movements history, not just its own pre-merge purchases -- the UX doc's explicit edge case ('recomputed stats after merge should reflect the combined interval history, not just the survivor's').

lib/catalog/manager.ts: archiveItem(id, archived: boolean) -- plain is_archived update, household-scoped. recategorizeItem(id, categorySlug) -- updates catalog_items.category_id ONLY; base_unit is never touched by this function (the sticky-unit invariant from S-09's spec: existing stock_movements.qty_base values were recorded against the item's CURRENT base_unit, so changing it would silently corrupt every historical quantity). Rejects an 'uncategorized' target slug server-side (same backstop commit_receipt() already applies to new_item category resolution).

app/catalog/page.tsx + catalog-manager.tsx ('use client'): a searchable/filterable list (active + archived, toggle to show archived) with per-item archive/unarchive and recategorize (category select) actions, plus a merge flow -- select two active items, choose the survivor via radio, see the preview counts, confirm. Linked from app/inventory/page.tsx (the UX journey's stated trigger: noticing a duplicate while browsing Inventory) and app/page.tsx's Today card.
out_of_scope: Auto-detecting likely-duplicate pairs to suggest a merge -- this story is the manual correction tool the UX doc describes as 'an occasional correction, not a routine maintenance task'; proactive duplicate detection is a future enhancement, not required by A12.
Merging more than two items in one operation -- the schema/RPC/UX are all pairwise; a third duplicate is a second merge.
Reassigning ingest_jobs or receipts rows -- neither references catalog_items directly (receipts contain receipt_lines, already handled via matched_item_id).
Any change to base_unit as part of recategorize -- see invariants; explicitly rejected, not just unimplemented.
acceptance: Merging two catalog items reassigns aliases and movements to the survivor and recomputes stats correctly (A12) -- verified with a fixture pair that BOTH have real purchase history at different intervals, confirming the survivor's post-merge item_stats (ewma_interval_days, purchase_count) reflects the combined history, not just its own pre-merge numbers, and that a subsequent purchase of either item's raw alias text resolves to the single surviving catalog_items row.
invariants: The loser is archived, never hard-deleted -- every table this function reassigns past (aliases, movements, price history, receipt lines, plan entries, shopping list items) keeps full referential integrity and audit history (ADR-0001).
base_unit is immutable via recategorize -- category_id is the only column that changes; historical qty_base values are never reinterpreted under a different unit.
purchase_count after a merge equals the sum of both items' pre-merge purchase_count, not just the survivor's -- the one stat recompute cannot derive on its own.

Every reassignment inside merge_catalog_items is scoped to p_household_id, even though single-household v1 makes cross-household collision unreachable today -- matches this repo's existing household-scoping convention everywhere else rather than being the one exception.
